Considering the set of vectors $\vvec=\twovec{-2}{1}$ and $\wvec = \twovec{8}{-4}$, we see that the vector $$ \bvec = 3\vvec + \wvec = \twovec2{-1} $$ is one vector in the span of the vectors $\vvec$ and $\wvec$ because it is a linear combination of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$.

To determine whether the vector $\bvec=\twovec{5}{2}$ is in the span of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$, we form the matrix $$ A = \begin{bmatrix} \vvec \amp \wvec \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \amp 8 \\ 1 \amp -4 \\ \end{bmatrix} $$ and consider the equation $A\xvec=\bvec$. We have $$ \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} -2 \amp 8 \amp 5 \\ 1 \amp -4 \amp 2 \\ \end{array} \right] \sim \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} 1 \amp -4 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right], $$ which shows that the equation $A\xvec = \bvec$ is inconsistent. Therefore, $\bvec=\twovec52$ is one vector that is not in the span of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$.
